assertions.title: Newsletter rendered at TOP position in email preview

steps.action: Seed profile, navigate to /promotion, expand Newsletter card
steps.expected: Newsletter card expanded with editor visible
steps.observed: Newsletter card expanded with heading field, position toggle, toolbar, and TipTap editor visible

steps.action: Fill date range 'Nov 28 - Dec 1', type newsletter body text, set heading to 'Store Updates', verify position toggle is Top
steps.observed: Preview generated successfully with newsletter section visible

steps.expected: HEADER → NEWSLETTER → BRAND SECTIONS → HOW TO SHOP → IMPORTANT NOTES → FOOTER → UNSUBSCRIBE
steps.observed: HEADER → NEWSLETTER → HOW TO SHOP → IMPORTANT NOTES → FOOTER → UNSUBSCRIBE (no brand sections since no discount entries were added at this point — ordering is correct relative to existing sections)

steps.observed: Bottom button has bg-primary class (active state), Top button has default styling

steps.action: Add discount entry '50% Off All Watches' to create brand sections
steps.observed: Preview shows discount entry in email

steps.expected: HEADER → BRAND SECTIONS → NEWSLETTER → HOW TO SHOP → IMPORTANT NOTES → FOOTER → UNSUBSCRIBE
steps.observed: HEADER (BLACK FRIDAY OUTLET EVENT) → BRAND SECTIONS (50% Off All Watches) → NEWSLETTER (Store Updates) → HOW TO SHOP → IMPORTANT NOTES → FOOTER → UNSUBSCRIBE — exact match

assertions.title: Newsletter body content with inline styles in email HTML

steps.action: Apply bold and italic formatting to newsletter body text, check HTML Code tab
steps.expected: Newsletter body HTML has all CSS as inline style attributes (e.g., font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;)
steps.observed: Newsletter body uses ... tags instead of inline style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;". The heading and container DO have inline styles. No

assertions.issues: Newsletter body formatting (bold, italic) uses semantic HTML tags (<strong>, <em>) rather than explicit inline CSS style attributes (style="font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;"). The assertion requires 'every visual property is inline (font-weight: bold, font-style: italic, etc.)'. While functionally equivalent for email clients, the implementation does not match the exact specification which calls for inline CSS style attributes. No <style> blocks or class references are present, which partially meets the requirement.

assertions.title: Empty newsletter does not render section in email

steps.action: Clear newsletter body (Ctrl+A, Backspace), verify editor is empty

steps.expected: No newsletter section visible in preview
steps.observed: Preview shows: HEADER → BRAND SECTIONS → HOW TO SHOP → IMPORTANT NOTES → FOOTER → UNSUBSCRIBE — no newsletter gap or content

steps.action: Check HTML Code tab for newsletter markup
steps.expected: No <!-- NEWSLETTER --> comment, no heading, no container, no empty placeholder
steps.observed: HTML contains no <!-- NEWSLETTER --> comment, no 'Store Updates' text, no 'newsletter' string — completely absent from generated HTML

summary: Tested 5 assertions: 4 passed, 1 failed (VAL-EMAIL-004: newsletter body formatting uses semantic HTML tags <strong>/<em> instead of inline CSS style attributes font-weight/font-style as specified in the validation contract)
